content:
Spotify has surpassed 300 million paid subscribers, marking a major milestone for the audio streaming service and signalling a new phase in its competition with Apple Music.

Spotify celebrates reaching 300 million paid subscribers

The company revealed the figure in its second-quarter results, reporting 300 million Premium subscribers, a 9% year-on-year increase, and 777 million monthly active users.

Spotify has gradually expanded its paid offering from pure music streaming into areas such as audiobooks and podcasts.

Apple has not published Apple Music subscriber numbers since the service crossed 60 million in 2019. It has, however, recently disclosed a much larger but very different milestone: 1.5 billion paid subscriptions.

That total covers Apple's own services, including Apple Music, iCloud+ and Apple TV. A significant portion, however, is believed to come from third-party app subscriptions sold through the App Store, on which Apple takes a 15% to 30% cut.

Both Spotify and Apple Music have raised prices this year. Spotify increased its US individual monthly plan from US$11.99 to US$12.99 in January, while Apple Music lifted its individual monthly fee from US$10.99 to US$11.99 last month.

Apple Music and Spotify are battling for users

Spotify's growth follows a string of new features and updates rolled out this year, including:

  • Taste Profile personalisation controls
  • SongDNA
  • Distraction-free mode
  • A redesigned iPad app
  • Video podcast upgrades
  • An AI mixing tool
  • Background download capability
  • Enhanced playlist pinning
  • Snapchat integration

Apple Music, meanwhile, will gain new features in iOS 27 next month, including redesigned artist and album pages, improved AutoMix transitions, faster playback speeds, a landscape "Now Playing" interface and Siri AI integration.
